title: The $10 Billion Tussle Over Walmart’s Credit Cards
summary: Walmart ended its nearly two-decade exclusive credit card partnership with Synchrony Financial, switching to Capital One Financial Corp. Walmart sought a larger share of revenue and more approved applicants from Synchrony, reflecting a broader trend where major retailers can demand better concessions from card companies. This shift highlights how the once-pervasive business of store credit cards is changing as traditional mall retail declines and banks compete for agreements with strong merchants like Amazon and Costco.

title: The $10 Billion Tussle Over Walmart’s Credit Cards
summary: Walmart ended its nearly two-decade-long exclusive partnership with Synchrony Financial for its credit cards, choosing Capital One instead. This move highlights a shift in the retail credit card industry, where large merchants like Walmart are demanding better terms from card issuers as traditional mall retailers decline. Banks are now competing fiercely for agreements with successful e-commerce focused retailers.

title: JD.com Unmanned Grocery Store Goes Live
summary: Online retailer JD.com Inc. has launched its first unmanned grocery store for general public use in Yantai, Shandong province, aiming for profitability within six months. This launch positions JD.com ahead of rivals Amazon.com and Alibaba in commercializing fully automated retail stores. The store utilizes advanced technologies like facial recognition and cloud computing, with plans for further expansion across China.

title: Exclusive | Hain Celestial’s brand overload behind grim sale prospects
summary: Hain Celestial Group is struggling to find a buyer despite being informally for sale for about a year. The company's founder, Irwin Simon, built an organic-foods powerhouse but expanded it to include too many brands, none large enough to entice a suitor at his asking price. Nestlé SA previously showed interest but reportedly conditioned an acquisition on Hain Celestial selling its low-margin chicken and turkey division.

title: Is Amazon's next target - Target?
summary: A Wall Street analyst suggests Amazon's next major brick-and-mortar acquisition could be Target, following its Whole Foods purchase. The proposed acquisition is based on shared demographics and a manageable store count, with an estimated valuation of $41 billion for Target. This speculation continues a trend of analysts predicting Amazon's future deals across various sectors.

title: Consumer Discretionary ETFs Head to Head: XLY vs. VCR
summary: This article compares two consumer discretionary ETFs, XLY and VCR, highlighting their exposure, holdings, and performance. Fueled by strong consumer demand and positive economic trends, the consumer discretionary sector is attracting significant investor attention. While XLY has higher AUM, VCR offers a cheaper expense ratio and greater diversification, with both showing similar performance.

title: Philips and American Well form global partnership in telehealth for consumer health and professional healthcare
summary: Royal Philips and American Well have announced a multi-year strategic partnership to integrate American Well’s virtual care capabilities into Philips’ digital health solutions globally. The collaboration aims to provide seamless consumer experiences in personal health, population health management, and clinical programs, starting with the Philips Avent uGrow parenting platform to offer 24/7 access to professional medical consultations. This partnership aligns with Philips' vision of coordinated care across the health continuum and will expand access to telehealth services for consumers and healthcare professionals.

title: Cardinal Health fires back at Amazon health-care threat: You can’t beat our prices
summary: Cardinal Health is challenging Amazon's potential entry into the health-care market, asserting that its scale and size give it an unbeatable price advantage in medical distribution. This comes as Amazon.com Inc. is reportedly considering a larger delve into health care, leveraging its reputation for low prices. Cardinal Health maintains that its established position makes it competitive in pricing for medical supplies.

title: Lost in space? Zuma satellite allegedly missing after SpaceX launch
summary: A $1 billion-plus communication satellite named Zuma, built by Northrop Grumman, is reportedly missing after its launch aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket on January 7th from Cape Canaveral. It's feared the secretive satellite may have failed to reach orbit. This incident follows several other SpaceX-related news items, including previous spy satellite launches and Falcon Heavy developments.

title: Amazon Rival JD.com Built the Equivalent of Monaco in Warehouse Space in Three Months
summary: JD.com Inc. significantly expanded its warehouse space, adding 2 million square meters (21.5 million square feet) in three months from July to September, an area equivalent to Monaco. This rapid expansion, rivaling Amazon's growth, is part of JD's strategy to build and control its own logistics chain for faster delivery and improved customer satisfaction, a different approach compared to Alibaba's past reliance on third-party shippers. The company operated 405 warehouses covering 9 million square meters at the end of September.

title: Vuzix launches first augmented reality sunglasses with Alexa integration at CES
summary: Vuzix Corporation unveiled the Vuzix Blade, the first augmented reality sunglasses with Amazon's Alexa voice assistant built-in, at CES 2018. These smart glasses feature a sleeker design, an 8-megapixel camera, and the Android operating system, allowing users to display various information within their field of vision and connect to the internet or smartphones. A developer version will be available for $1,997, with a consumer version expected in Q2 for $1,000, aiming for a price under $500 in future iterations.

title: Walmart expanding ‘Scan & Go’ mobile checkout to 100 more stores this month
summary: Walmart is expanding its Mobile Express Scan & Go app to 100 additional stores, bringing the total to 125 Walmart locations in 33 states. This initiative allows customers to scan, bag, and pay for items directly using a mobile phone, bypassing traditional checkout lines. The expansion follows a successful rollout at Sam's Club stores and aims to streamline the shopping experience despite potential challenges like customer adoption and increased shrink.

title: Amazon's aggressive poaching tactics in Israel have start-ups threatening to abandon AWS
summary: Amazon's aggressive recruitment of employees from Israeli start-ups, including Lemonade, is causing some companies to threaten to abandon Amazon Web Services (AWS). Lemonade co-founder Shai Wininger voiced his frustration publicly, prompting Amazon CTO Werner Vogels to investigate the issue, suggesting it might involve sourcing agencies. This tension highlights a broader conflict between Amazon and its smaller tech partners, potentially pushing companies towards rival cloud providers.

title: SoundHound Brings Voice Interaction to Hyundai Cars
summary: SoundHound's independent voice assistant, Hound, will be integrated into Hyundai cars starting in 2019, providing in-car voice control for various features and smart home interaction. This move highlights the growing traction of independent voice AI solutions in the automotive industry, offering car manufacturers more control over user experience compared to Amazon Alexa or Google Assistant. SoundHound is also expanding its presence to other devices beyond the car, demonstrating the increasing role of independent voice technology companies.

title: Cramer shares 5 reasons why the retail sector is back in action, according to industry executives
summary: Jim Cramer identified five key factors contributing to the resurgence of the retail sector, challenging Wall Street's skepticism. These factors include a stronger consumer base, millennials starting families, effective on- and offline strategies from traditional retailers, market share gains by surviving companies, and undervalued stock valuations in some retail giants like Nordstrom and Macy's. Cramer suggests that the sector is now "investable" after years of decline.

title: Equinix to Build More Owned Data Centers with “Nodes” for Cloud Giants
summary: Equinix plans to build more owned data centers with 1MW to 2MW "nodes" specifically for hyper-scale cloud and SaaS providers, including Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform, Facebook, and Apple. This strategy aims to capture the next wave of cloud deployments and secure competitive advantage by attracting profitable enterprise customers, despite lower margins compared to retail cabinet deployments. The company also continues its M&A strategy, including recent acquisitions of Verizon data centers and Metronode in Australia, expanding its global footprint.

title: A lesson about self awareness from PagerDuty cofounder Alex Solomon
summary: This article highlights Alex Solomon, cofounder of PagerDuty, and his unique act of self-awareness in stepping down as CEO to allow for more experienced leadership as the company scaled. Solomon's decision, driven by the company's rapid growth and his desire to focus on product, showcases an uncommon humility among startup founders. The move allowed PagerDuty to continue its strong growth trajectory under new leadership.

title: Sprouts Farmers Market may open a third San Antonio store
summary: Sprouts Farmers Market Inc. is considering opening a third store in San Antonio, according to a state filing, with construction slated for July 2018 at the intersection of Bulverde Road and E. Evans Road. The expansion comes as the San Antonio grocery market intensifies with new H-E-B stores, the entry of Lidl, and Amazon’s acquisition of Whole Foods. Sprouts previously closed a San Antonio store in 2015, which is now a Planet Fitness.

title: Lemonade Co-Founder Calls Out Amazon for Poaching Employees
summary: Lemonade Co-Founder Shai Wininger publicly accused Amazon of poaching his employees through social media posts, even threatening to leave Amazon's AWS cloud platform. He argued that Amazon's tactics, including offering "obscene amounts of money," breach trust with startup customers and threaten Israel's tech ecosystem. Amazon CTO Werner Vogels responded, suggesting it might be a sourcing agency issue and offering to investigate.

title: These Internet Stocks Are Red Hot
summary: Despite rapid growth in stock price and concerns over inflated valuations, Morgan Stanley analyst Brian Nowak identifies nine hot tech stocks, including Alphabet, Facebook, and Amazon, that are expected to continue their strong performance in 2018 and beyond. The article details growth projections, financial figures, and specific catalysts for each company, emphasizing innovation, market dominance, and strategic investments as key drivers of their continued success in the internet sector.

title: Amazon Begins to Act as Its Own Freight Broker
summary: Amazon.com Inc. has begun to directly broker freight to truck drivers, marking a significant step into the transportation and logistics industry beyond its previous reliance on third-party firms. The e-commerce giant registered as a freight broker in 2016 and has since brokered a small number of loads, indicating its intent to gradually control more of its supply chain. This move builds on Amazon's earlier actions, such as becoming a nonvessel operating common carrier and freight forwarder, aiming to cut out middlemen and enhance its logistics efficiency.

title: Convenience Stores Are Getting Squeezed by Fast Food and Dollar Stores
summary: The U.S. convenience store industry is facing increasing pressure from various competitors, including fast-food restaurants, supermarkets, dollar stores, and Amazon.com Inc. This intense competition is impacting merchandise sales growth, which is the weakest since 2013, and is pushing gas-station retail chains towards consolidation and diversification of their offerings.

title: Could this company become Chicago's own Salesforce?
summary: Relativity, a Chicago-based legal software company, has grown into a significant player in the e-discovery market, used by almost all of the nation's largest law firms. Led by CEO Andrew Sieja, the company is often compared to Salesforce for its platform approach and is considered a "unicorn" with potential IPO prospects. Despite being a dominant player, Relativity faces challenges from cloud-native rivals and has recently launched its own cloud product to stay competitive.

title: Netflix Has Record-Breaking Fourth Quarter In 2017, Exceeds $11B In Revenue
summary: Netflix announced a record-breaking fourth quarter and a strong 2017, exceeding $11 billion in streaming revenue and adding 24 million new memberships globally. Despite facing unexpected expenses like a $39 million non-cash charge for unreleased content, the company surpassed its contribution profit and operating income forecasts due to higher-than-expected member growth. Netflix plans to increase its content spending to $7.5-$8 billion in 2018 and marketing spend to approximately $2 billion to drive further growth and retain its competitive edge amidst rising competition.

title: Retail and Ecommerce Distribution Center Roundup
summary: This article provides a roundup of recent distribution and fulfillment center activities in the domestic market, detailing new openings, leases, and closures by various companies. Key players like Amazon, Best Buy, IKEA, and Ulta Beauty are expanding their logistics footprints to support both retail and ecommerce operations. The report highlights significant investments in new facilities across several states, indicating growth in the sector.

title: Kimberly-Clark to cut 5,000 jobs on sluggish sales partly due to fewer babies
summary: Kimberly-Clark plans to cut 5,000 to 5,500 jobs, representing 12% to 13% of its workforce, and slash costs by $1.5 billion over the next four years due to sluggish sales. The company attributes this decline partly to lower birthrates in key markets like the U.S. and South Korea, impacting demand for products like Huggies. Despite a 22% increase in profit, sales rose only 1%, prompting a major restructuring to improve competitiveness and profitability.

title: ETFs powered by artificial intelligence are getting smarter, says fund co-founder
summary: Exchange-traded funds (ETFs) that use artificial intelligence are becoming more sophisticated, according to Art Amador, co-founder of EquBot. The AI-Powered Equity ETF (AIEQ), which launched in October, aims to outperform the market using AI algorithms. Amador highlights the AI's ability to process vast amounts of data autonomously and continuously improve, mimicking a team of equity research analysts.

title: Walmart job cuts to total nearly 1,000 at Bentonville HQ
summary: Walmart Inc. is implementing job cuts totaling nearly 1,000 positions at its Bentonville headquarters as part of an effort to streamline operations against competition from Amazon. The first wave of layoffs impacted 400-500 jobs across various divisions, with a second phase anticipated in 2019 during a headquarters consolidation. Despite the cuts, Walmart is also taking steps to retain employees, such as boosting hourly wages and creating new roles in its online grocery business.

title: Shanghai Roastery opened as the world's 'highest-grossing Starbucks,' CEO says
summary: The Starbucks Reserve Roastery Shanghai has been declared the world's highest-grossing Starbucks by CEO Kevin Johnson. The roastery averaged more than double the transactions of the Seattle Roastery and achieved an average order value of $29. This large-format store represents a significant success for Starbucks in the Chinese market.

title: Sysco Feasts On Economies Of Scale For Strong Competitive Advantage
summary: Sysco (SYY) leverages its extensive distribution network and economies of scale to achieve consistent profit growth, strong margins, and a leading market share in the food industry. Despite its strong fundamentals, international expansion opportunities, and an impressive yield, the stock's valuation appears to be undervalued. The article highlights SYY's consistent NOPAT growth, proper executive compensation alignment with ROIC, and its competitive advantage against rivals and potential threats like Amazon/Whole Foods.

title: Keurig to take control of Dr Pepper Snapple in $18.7 billion deal
authors: ['Jennifer Kaplan and Lisa Wolfson', 'Eric Pfanner Bloomberg News']
summary: JAB Holding's Keurig Green Mountain business has agreed to acquire Dr Pepper Snapple Group in an $18.7 billion deal. This acquisition seeks to create a massive beverage distribution network in the United States, allowing the new entity, Keurig Dr Pepper, to compete with major players like Coca-Cola and PepsiCo with an estimated annual revenue of $11 billion. The merger aims to leverage the combined strengths of both companies in e-commerce and traditional retail channels to enhance market share in coffee and soft drinks.

title: Amazon, Berkshire Hathaway and JPMorgan Team Up to Try to Disrupt Health Care (Published 2018)
authors: ['Nick Wingfield Katie Thomas and Reed Abelson']
summary: Amazon, Berkshire Hathaway, and JPMorgan Chase announced the formation of an independent health care company for their U.S. employees. This alliance signals corporate frustration with rising health care costs and aims to disrupt the inefficient health care industry. The news caused a significant drop in the stock prices of major health insurance companies.

title: Casey’s General Stores lets customers pay with Amazon Cash
summary: Casey's General Stores has partnered with Blackhawk Network to allow customers to pay for purchases using Amazon Cash. This initiative aims to serve both unbanked consumers and those who prefer not to use debit or credit cards, acting like a gift certificate system where users can load between $15 and $500 onto an Amazon Balance. The move highlights Amazon's broader strategy to expand its presence in digital payments and reach a wider demographic.

title: Amazon, Berkshire Hathaway and JP Morgan Chase join forces to tackle employees’ health-care costs
summary: Amazon, Berkshire Hathaway, and JP Morgan Chase announced a partnership to create an independent company focused on reining in health-care costs for their U.S. employees. This collaboration aims to address the rising health-care expenses faced by these three giant and influential employers.

title: Amazon, JPMorgan, Berkshire to create own health-care company
summary: Amazon, JPMorgan, and Berkshire Hathaway are partnering to create an independent health-care company focused on providing quality, affordable care for their U.S. employees. The venture aims to tackle the rising costs of health care, initially focusing on technology for transparent care. This move caused shares in health care companies to drop, as Amazon's entry into the sector has been highly anticipated.

title: The company that made coffee pods ubiquitous just dropped $18 billion on Dr. Pepper
summary: Keurig Green Mountain, known for its K-cups, has acquired an 87% stake in Dr. Pepper Snapple Group for $18.7 billion. This strategic move aims to leverage Dr. Pepper Snapple's extensive brick-and-mortar distribution network, expanding Keurig's market reach beyond online channels. The acquisition also positions Keurig to directly compete with major beverage companies like Coca-Cola and PepsiCo while challenging Starbucks' retail presence.

title: Starbucks executive pay: Schultz gets $18M as Starbucks bulks up private security
summary: Howard Schultz, Executive Chairman of Starbucks, received a total compensation of $17.98 million, despite a significant drop from the previous year. This compensation included an 60 percent increase in personal security. The article details the breakdown of Schultz's compensation and notes the company's increased spending on private security.

title: Amazon, JPMorgan Chase and Berkshire Hathaway to form their own healthcare tech company
summary: Amazon, JPMorgan Chase, and Berkshire Hathaway announced a partnership to form an independent healthcare company focused on technology solutions for their U.S. employees. The goal is to provide high-quality, transparent healthcare at a reasonable cost, free from traditional profit-making incentives. Led by key executives from each company, this venture aims to address the complex and costly U.S. healthcare system.

title: Amazon, Berkshire Hathaway And JPMorgan Chase Launch New Health Care Company : The Two-Way
summary: Amazon, Berkshire Hathaway, and JPMorgan Chase are teaming up to create a new healthcare company designed to cut costs and improve employee satisfaction with healthcare plans. The venture aims to provide high-quality healthcare for their U.S. employees at a lower cost, operating "free from profit-making incentives and constraints." The initial focus will be on technology solutions, with the ultimate goal of benefiting all Americans.

title: Into the woods: Columbia Sportswear adopts Microsoft cloud
summary: Columbia Sportswear has adopted Microsoft's cloud services, including Dynamics 365 and Azure, to enhance customer experience, personalize interactions, and improve omnichannel capabilities. The move aims to drive insights from various consumer touchpoints and addresses the retail industry's increasing dependence on customer data analysis. This strategy allows Columbia to better understand customer desires and manage data at a rapid pace in an evolving retail landscape.

title: Alibaba earnings: Singles Day was a hit, but logistics and cloud will also be in focus
summary: Alibaba's Singles Day event was a record-breaking success, with gross merchandise volume exceeding $25 billion, up 39% from the previous year. This momentum is expected to significantly boost Alibaba's sales for its December quarter earnings report on Feb. 1. Beyond the holiday shopping success, investors will also be looking at the performance of the company's logistics and cloud segments.

title: What to make of Amazon and Warren Buffett’s mystery health care project
summary: Amazon, JPMorgan Chase, and Warren Buffett announced a new health care initiative aimed at improving employee satisfaction and reducing costs, sending shockwaves through the industry. The venture's details are sparse, but experts speculate on self-insurance strategies, improved digital infrastructure, and potentially disrupting traditional health care providers. The announcement caused a significant drop in stock prices for pharmacy-benefit managers and health insurers, reflecting market anxiety about potentially disruptive changes.
